provenance.title: NEO: NeRF It Once, Edit It Many Times for Continuous Object Manipulation
affiliations: Institute of Robotics and Machine Intelligence, Poznan University of Technology
provenance.abstract: We present NEO, a unified framework providing language-guided NeRF editing for robotic manipulation. It introduces (i) language-guided object removal via neural field resampling with multiview-consistent progressive inpainting, (ii) direct NeRF weight editing via knowledge distillation composing original and edited NeRFs through a teacher-student model, and (iii) the NEO-Dataset, the first benchmark for quantitatively evaluating NeRF scene editing for robot manipulation.
key_claims: A unified NeRF editing framework that directly updates network weights for realistic, geometrically consistent, and persistent scene modifications without re-scanning
A scene-focused knowledge distillation method that reconfigures scenes by composing an original NeRF and an edited NeRF via a teacher-student model
The NEO-Dataset benchmark: 12 registered pre/post-edit tabletop scenes for quantitative NeRF-editing evaluation
Outperforms DFF, NeRFiller, and Seal-3D baselines on object removal and pick-and-place manipulation in PSNR/SSIM/RMSE/reprojection-error metrics
Demonstrates persistent multi-step (assembly) editing where the same edited representation is reused as input to subsequent edits

architecture.primary_variant: NEO (full model: neural field resampling + progressive inpainting + teacher-student reconfiguration + language field update)

modules.name: F_Theta (base joint scene+language NeRF)
modules.output_shape: S in R^4 (density+RGB) and L in R^{d_l} (language feature), queried per continuous 3D point
modules.notes: Exact backbone (MLP vs hash-grid) not specified; see implementation_assumptions.

modules.name: Language field grounding / bounding-box retrieval
modules.input_shape: text prompt embedding phi(p) in R^{d_l}; language feature field L(x)
modules.output_shape: oriented bounding box b=(c,theta), c in R^3, theta in SO(2)

parameters.method: cosine similarity over surface points -> clustering -> largest cluster fit to oriented box

modules.notes: Clustering algorithm (e.g. DBSCAN vs k-means) not specified.

modules.name: Neural Field Resampling (Object Removal)
modules.input_shape: camera poses, oriented bounding box b, densities along ray
modules.output_shape: resampled ray densities/weights excluding samples inside b

parameters.stages: uniform resample over concatenated ray segments, then PDF-based hierarchical resample

modules.notes: Fixed sample counts for each of the two sampling stages not given numerically.

modules.name: Multiview-Consistent Progressive Inpainting
modules.input_shape: virtual object-centered renderings I_v tiled 2x2, original images I_o, masks M_v/M_o
modules.output_shape: inpainted composite images split back into per-view completions

parameters.view_augmentation: virtual hemisphere at bbox center, 4 azimuths, upward spiral of elevations

modules.notes: Exact count of virtual viewpoints and re-render interval n not given numerically.

modules.name: Mask-conditioned NeRF F~_Theta (edited/removed-object NeRF)
modules.output_shape: edited NeRF encoding scene with object removed and occluded regions reconstructed

modules.name: Density Regularization (anti-reappearance)
modules.input_shape: predicted densities sigma~ at sample points p
modules.output_shape: penalized density field with near-zero density inside b

parameters.formula: L_reg penalizes non-zero density predictions within bounding box b

modules.name: Object Reconfiguration / Knowledge Distillation (teacher-student)
modules.input_shape: F_Theta (teacher, outside-bbox and relocated-object regions), F~_Theta (teacher, inside removal bbox), virtual object-centered views I_v
modules.output_shape: student NeRF F_hat_Theta (parameters Theta_hat) encoding reconfigured scene S'

parameters.stages: phase 1: direct field (density/color) supervision; phase 2: + volumetric RGB and depth image supervision

modules.notes: Differs from Seal-3D by using region-wise composition from multiple teachers rather than a single fully-edited teacher.

modules.name: Language Field Update
modules.input_shape: images rendered from fixed F_hat_Theta at original camera poses Omega
modules.notes: Converges in 'a small number of iterations' (not quantified).

modules.name: Grasp Planning (AnyGrasp, external)
modules.input_shape: bounding box b / updated scene geometry
modules.notes: Treated as an off-the-shelf external component, not re-derived by this paper.

modules.name: Editable NEO Model Orchestrator (Editing Many Times)
modules.output_shape: (S',L') reused as input for subsequent edits

parameters.invariant: resulting representation retains same structure as original input, enabling reuse

connections.to: Editable NEO Model Orchestrator (Editing Many Times)

connections.from: Editable NEO Model Orchestrator (Editing Many Times)
connections.tensor_name: (S',L') fed back as (S,L) for next edit

differences.description: All components enabled: virtual view distribution, 2x2 grid inpainting, mask-conditioned training, full L_distill.

differences.removed: virtual object-centered view augmentation during inpainting/distillation
2x2 grid tiling strategy for diffusion inpainting
mask conditioning M in NeRF reconstruction loss

differences.changed: student trained only with first term of L_distill (density/color along rays), no RGB/depth image supervision

data_augmentation: Virtual object-centered camera views synthesized on a hemisphere around the removed-object bounding box (4 azimuths, upward spiral of elevations) to concentrate supervision on previously occluded surfaces
training_pipeline.curriculum: Progressive inpainting: virtual object-centered views are re-rendered every n steps and re-inpainted; the diffusion inpainting strength factor xi is decreased after each iteration so later iterations preserve more of the current rendering, promoting convergence.

datasets.name: NEO-Dataset (proposed benchmark)
datasets.split: 11 single-object scenes + 1 multi-object scene, pre/post-edit registered via ArUco markers

special_conditions: Scene inpainting timing: NEO ~6 min vs DFF ~13 min vs NeRFiller ~1.5 hr (~15x speed-up)
Object manipulation timing: NEO ~1.5 min vs Seal-3D ~3 min (~2x speed-up)
Two robotic arm setups used for scene capture (Franka Emika Panda and UR5)

implementation_assumptions.assumption: Base NeRF backbone is a modern efficient representation (e.g. Instant-NGP-style hash-grid MLP) rather than the original vanilla MLP NeRF, given emphasis on fast (minute-scale) editing/training times.
implementation_assumptions.basis: inferred from results (sub-2-hour full pipeline timings reported for inpainting and distillation)

implementation_assumptions.assumption: Optimizer is Adam (or AdamW), the near-universal default for NeRF and diffusion-adjacent training.

Diffusion inpainting model is Stable Diffusion, as explicitly labeled in Fig. 6's caption, likely used with an inpainting-specific checkpoint/pipeline (e.g. SD inpainting variant) rather than base text-to-image SD.
implementation_assumptions.basis: explicitly named in figure caption; specific checkpoint/version not stated in main text

implementation_assumptions.assumption: Loss weighting constants lambda_rec and lambda_reg in L_masked are assumed roughly equal (e.g. both ~1.0) absent stated values.
implementation_assumptions.basis: inferred / common practice for combined reconstruction+regularization objectives

implementation_assumptions.assumption: Re-render interval n (iterative inpainting refresh) is on the order of hundreds of training iterations (e.g. ~250-500).
implementation_assumptions.basis: inferred from typical NeRF-refinement-with-inpainting literature (e.g. NeRFiller-style loops)

implementation_assumptions.assumption: Virtual viewpoint count for the object-centered hemisphere augmentation is approximately 8-16 views (4 azimuths x 2-4 elevation steps in the spiral).
implementation_assumptions.basis: inferred from qualitative description ('four opposing azimuths and varying elevations, forming a short upward spiral')

implementation_assumptions.assumption: Language field embeddings d_l correspond to CLIP embedding dimensionality (e.g. 512 or 768), consistent with prior LERF-style language fields the paper builds on.
implementation_assumptions.basis: inferred from prior work (LERF [14]) and explicit later use of CLIP for language field update

implementation_assumptions.assumption: Framework is PyTorch, consistent with the vast majority of contemporary NeRF/diffusion research codebases (e.g. nerfstudio-based).

ambiguities.description: Exact NeRF backbone architecture (network depth/width, positional encoding, hash-grid vs MLP) is never specified in the text or figures.
Number of virtual viewpoints sampled on the hemisphere ('four opposing azimuths and varying elevations, forming a short upward spiral') is described qualitatively but no exact count is given.
Numeric values of the loss weighting constants lambda_rec and lambda_reg in L_masked are not provided anywhere in the paper.

The re-render interval n ('virtual object-centered views I_v are re-rendered every n steps') is referenced symbolically but never assigned a numeric value; total number of inpainting iterations and the exact decay schedule of the inpainting strength factor xi are likewise unspecified.
ambiguities.primary_assumption: n on the order of a few hundred iterations; xi linearly decayed from 1.0 toward a small residual value across iterations

ambiguities.description: The paper spans robotics (manipulation), computer vision (NeRF/3D reconstruction), and language grounding (CLIP/DINO language fields); the fixed SIR domain enum has no 'Robotics' category, so classification is inherently approximate.
The 'fixed number of uniform samples' and the 'second, fixed set of samples' for the two-stage neural field resampling procedure are referenced but no numeric sample counts are given.
ambiguities.primary_assumption: 64 uniform + 128 hierarchical samples per ray (typical NeRF defaults)
